nodes.summary: For a convex loss `L`, `L ∘ μ[W | m]` is integrable whenever `W` and `L ∘ W` are.
nodes.title: Integrability of a convex loss of a conditional expectation

nodes.summary: For a convex loss `L` and an integrable `W` with integrable loss, `∫ L(μ[W | m]) dμ ≤ ∫ L(W) dμ`.
nodes.title: Rao–Blackwell inequality for one law

nodes.summary: Conditioning leaves the squared-error risk at `c` unchanged if and only if `W` already equals `μ[W | m]` almost everywhere.
nodes.title: Equality case under squared error

nodes.summary: For `W` with a finite second moment and any target `c`, `E (W - c)² = E (μ[W | m] - c)² + E (W - μ[W | m])²`. This is the Pythagorean identity `MeasureTheory.integral_sq_sub_eq_integral_sq_sub_condExp_add` with the constant predictor `fun _ => c`, with the two summands commuted; it is not a second Pythagorean proof.
nodes.title: Squared-error decomposition

nodes.summary: If the statistic `T` is sufficient for `P` and `W` is a measurable estimator with finite second moment under every `P θ`, there is a measurable `φ` such that `φ ∘ T` is a version of every `E_θ[W | T]`, has the same mean as `W`, and for every target `τ θ` satisfies `E_θ (W - τ θ)² = E_θ (φ(T) - τ θ)² + E_θ (W - φ(T))²`.
nodes.title: The Rao–Blackwell theorem for a sufficient statistic

nodes.summary: Let `m` be sufficient for the family of probability measures `P`, and let `W` be a measurable estimator that is integrable under every `P θ`. There is one parameter-free `m`-measurable estimator `η`, a version of `P_θ[W | m]` for every `θ`, with the same mean as `W` under every `θ` and no larger risk under every loss `ℓ θ` that is convex in the estimate (for which `ℓ θ ∘ W` is integrable).
nodes.title: The Rao–Blackwell theorem
